messages:
maria: Quick smoke on new hatchery-embed v1.2 bring-up. Short summary: recall@1 down ~5% vs beech-embed-v2 on our long-tail holdout (rare queries). Numbers pasted below.
kevin: can you paste the exact eval command + model tags? :eyes: 
maria: sure — ran `eval-embed --model hatchery-1.2 --holdout longtail --k 1,5,10 --metric recall` on staging. output:
```
recall@1: 0.71 (beech-v2: 0.76)
recall@5: 0.89 (beech-v2: 0.90)
recall@10: 0.93 (beech-v2: 0.94)
```
Also noticed more id-flips in nearest-neighbor set for queries with <5 tokens.
deploy-bot: hatchery-1.2 deployed to staging (pool: dev-embeddings)
sasha: low-token queries often show tokenizer mismatch — did you normalize casing / punctuation consistently between corpus/index and query embedding? 
maria: index used default pipeline (lowercase, strip punctuation). Query path used same code path but I will double-check tokenization artifacts. I saw cluster drift in UMAP plots — pushing a screenshot: <link>
alan: two quick hypotheses: 1) model produces lower-norm vectors for short queries -> cosine penalizes; 2) quantization profile (we used int8 per-tensor during build) amplifies small vector differences.
lina: i can repro local with both int8-per-tensor and int8-per-channel. my plan: run `embed-sweep --models hatchery-1.2{fp16,int8-per-tensor,int8-per-channel,int4}` over the holdout and compare recall/ID-flip rate and vector norm distributions.
maria: thanks. Also try L2-normalization at index-time vs runtime (we currently store raw vectors and cosine via normalized similarity). small bug: indexing pipeline missed whitening step used for beech-v2.
kevin: add PCA whitening as a config toggle (we have that in `index-config.yml`) — please enable for the test.
eval-bot: scheduled job 4592: `embed-sweep` started (params: hatchery-1.2,int8-per-channel,k=1,5,10,holdout=longtail)
sasha: good. also check tokenizer vocab differences — hatchery uses BPE 50k vs beech 30k. that can fragment short queries.
maria: sample short query failures:
- "refund" -> expected returns category page doc_332 but top-1 returns doc_278 (different intent)
- "reset password" -> top-1 ok but top-2 drops relevant docs
alan: if norms are lower for short queries, try scaling via learned scale per-length bucket as quick patch.
lina: running now. ETA ~20m.
maria: if int8-per-channel closes the gap, we can update quant profile in the onboarding PR. If not, might need retrain/regression with augmented short-query samples.
kevin: create a brief incident-style ticket if we see regression >3% recall@1; link to onboarding PR. :+1:
maria: will open ticket ENG-ML-4927 with logs and plots once sweep finishes. thanks all.
lina: sweep done — initial numbers: int8-per-channel recall@1=0.74, int8-per-tensor=0.70, int4=0.69, fp16=0.76. per-channel looks promising (closer to beech).
maria: great — can someone sanity-check vector norm hist plots I uploaded? link
sasha: looks like fp16 & per-channel norms nearly overlap; per-tensor skewed downwards for short queries. I'll put a quick note in the PR recommending per-channel quant.
kevin: next steps: (1) update quant profile to per-channel in the staging build (2) re-run full holdout and cluster stability check (UMAP + silhouette) (3) open rollback guard in console if recall drops in canary.
maria: agreed. I'll draft the PR and tag infra for canary policy. thanks everyone. :rocket:
